chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who takes dirhams to perform Hajj on behalf of another man. Is it permissible for him to spend from them on other than Hajj? He said: If he guarantees the Hajj, then the dirhams are for him; he does with them what he likes, and upon him is the performance of the Hajj.
ai.seo_question: Can a Hajj representative spend the given funds on other expenses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial autonomy of the Hajj representative (na'ib), establishing that upon guaranteeing the performance of the ritual, the funds become his personal property (mal) to utilize as he wishes, even if spent on other needs. This ruling highlights the distinction between the obligation of the act and the ownership of the resources, a key principle in Shia fiqh for understanding agency (wakalah) in religious duties. It underscores that the validity of the Hajj rests on the fulfillment of the rite rather than the specific allocation of the provided funds.
